# Ryman IT Asset Management Dashboard  
## Streamlit Project Specification (Source of Truth)

**Version:** 1.0  
**Status:** Design / pre-implementation  
**Audience:** Future developer / implementer  
**Related data:** Synthetic ServiceNow-style asset data generated by `ryman-asset-generator.py` and optionally loaded into Supabase (`ryman_assets` table)

This document is the **only authoritative specification** for building the Streamlit dashboard.  
Do not invent pages, metrics, or behaviours that contradict this document unless explicitly agreed.

---

## 1. Purpose & Alignment with the Role

The dashboard exists to demonstrate the day-to-day analytical and investigative work of an **Asset Management Analyst** at an organisation that manages thousands of technology assets (laptops, tablets, mobile phones, monitors, accessories) across many sites in New Zealand and Australia.

It must make the following role activities visible, interactive, and actionable:

1. Managing the full lifecycle of technology assets (planning → purchase → use → refresh → disposal)
2. Maintaining accurate asset records and detecting data-quality problems
3. Investigating missing, unassigned, under-utilised, and non-compliant assets
4. Analysing asset, procurement, and utilisation data to identify cost-saving opportunities, reduce waste, and support budgeting / forecasting
5. Producing reports and insights that support decision-making by Technology, Finance, Procurement, and village stakeholders

The dashboard is a **demonstration / portfolio tool**. It must feel realistic to someone who has done the job, while remaining simple enough to run locally or on Streamlit Community Cloud.

---

## 2. Design Principles

- **Role-first, not chart-first.** Every page and visual must answer a question an Asset Management Analyst (or their stakeholders) would actually ask.
- **Actionable over decorative.** Prefer tables that can be filtered/exported and clear KPI cards over purely aesthetic charts.
- **Data-quality visible.** Surface blanks, duplicates, anomalies, and non-compliance prominently rather than hiding them.
- **Site-aware.** The organisation has many villages + a head office. Location is a first-class dimension.
- **Lifecycle-aware.** Assets move through stages; the UI should make stage, age, and refresh timing obvious.
- **Two data modes.** The app must work with:
  - Local CSV (`ryman_assets.csv`) — zero configuration, good for demos offline
  - Supabase (`ryman_assets` table) — when credentials are present
- **Fast to understand.** A hiring manager or stakeholder should grasp the value of the tool within 60–90 seconds of opening it.

---

## 3. Technology Stack (Recommended)

| Layer | Choice | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Framework | Streamlit | Multi-page app (`pages/` directory) |
| Data access | pandas + optional `supabase` Python client | CSV always available; Supabase when env vars set |
| Charts | Plotly (preferred) or Altair | Interactive, exportable |
| Tables | `st.dataframe` / `st.data_editor` (read-only for demo) | Filtering, sorting, download |
| Config | `.streamlit/config.toml` + environment variables | Theme, wide mode |
| Secrets | Streamlit secrets or `.env` | Supabase URL + service role key |
| Deployment target | Local + Streamlit Community Cloud | Keep dependencies light |

**Out of scope for v1:** user authentication, write-back to ServiceNow/Supabase, real-time streaming, mobile-native UI.

---

## 4. Data Contract

### 4.1 Source of truth fields

The dashboard must be built against the column set produced by `ryman-asset-generator.py` (and mirrored in the Supabase table). Key columns and their intended use:

| Column | Type | Primary use in dashboard |
|--------|------|---------------------------|
| `sys_id` | text | Unique key, internal |
| `asset_tag` | text | Human-readable ID, tables, search |
| `serial_number` | text | Data-quality checks, duplicate detection |
| `ci_name` / `model` / `manufacturer` | text | Grouping, filters, model standardisation |
| `asset_type` | text | Primary category filter & breakdowns |
| `install_status` | text | Missing / In Stock / Installed etc. |
| `state` | text | Supporting status |
| `lifecycle_stage` | text | Lifecycle page, funnel, refresh planning |
| `assigned_to` | text | Unassigned investigation |
| `location` | text | Site-level views, remote audit simulation |
| `department` | text | Secondary dimension |
| `purchase_date` | date | Age, cohort, spend by period |
| `purchase_cost_nzd` | numeric | All cost & savings calculations |
| `po_number` | text | Procurement linkage |
| `warranty_expiration` / `warranty_status` | date / text | Risk & compliance |
| `encryption_status` | text | Compliance |
| `os_supported` | text | Compliance |
| `is_non_compliant` | boolean | Compliance KPI & lists |
| `last_discovered` | timestamp | Utilisation, stale assets |
| `days_since_last_seen` | int | Utilisation scoring |
| `utilisation_score` | int (0–100) | Under-utilised detection |
| `useful_life_years` | int | Refresh modelling |
| `planned_refresh_date` / `refresh_year` | date / int | Forecasting |
| `remaining_life_years` | numeric | Forecasting |
| `disposal_date` / `disposal_method` / `residual_value_nzd` | date / text / numeric | End-of-life & recovery value |
| `notes` | text | Investigation context |

### 4.2 Derived fields the app should calculate (do not require them in the source CSV)

- `asset_age_years` — from `purchase_date`
- `is_unassigned` — `assigned_to` is null/blank
- `is_missing` — `install_status == "Missing"`
- `is_underutilised` — `utilisation_score < 30` (configurable threshold)
- `is_stale` — `days_since_last_seen > 90` (configurable)
- `is_past_warranty` — `warranty_status == "Expired"` or date logic
- `estimated_idle_cost` — simple heuristic (e.g. annual cost of capital or residual opportunity on low-utilisation / unassigned devices)
- `refresh_cohort` — based on `refresh_year` or remaining life bands

### 4.3 Data loading rules

1. On startup, attempt Supabase if `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are present and valid.
2. Fall back to local `ryman_assets.csv` (path configurable).
3. Show a clear data-source indicator in the sidebar (“Source: Supabase” / “Source: Local CSV”).
4. Cache the loaded dataframe (Streamlit cache) with a manual “Refresh data” button.
5. Never modify the source data in place for the demo; all filters are view-level.

## 5. Information Architecture (Pages)

Use Streamlit multipage structure:

```
app/
├── Home.py                    # or streamlit_app.py
├── pages/
│   ├── 1_Executive_Overview.py
│   ├── 2_Asset_Inventory.py
│   ├── 3_Data_Quality_&_Anomalies.py
│   ├── 4_Missing_Unassigned_Underutilised.py
│   ├── 5_Lifecycle_&_Refresh.py
│   ├── 6_Cost_Savings_&_Forecasting.py
│   └── 7_Compliance_&_Risk.py
└── utils/
    ├── data_loader.py
    ├── metrics.py
    └── charts.py
```

Suggested navigation labels (sidebar):

1. Executive Overview  
2. Asset Inventory  
3. Data Quality & Anomalies  
4. Missing / Unassigned / Under-utilised  
5. Lifecycle & Refresh Planning  
6. Cost Savings & Forecasting  
7. Compliance & Risk  

Optional future page (v2): Site Audit Simulator (pick a village and generate an audit checklist).

---

## 6. Global UI Elements (every page)

### Sidebar (persistent)

- Data source indicator + last refresh timestamp
- “Refresh data” button
- Global filters (apply across most pages where sensible):
  - Asset type (multi-select)
  - Location / Region (NZ vs AU + individual sites, or multi-select)
  - Lifecycle stage or Install status
  - Date range on `purchase_date` (optional)
- Utilisation threshold slider (default 30) — used by under-utilised logic
- Stale threshold slider (default 90 days)
- Download current filtered dataset (CSV)
- Short “About this demo” expander explaining synthetic data and role alignment

### Top of main area

- Page title + one-sentence purpose
- Optional KPI row (3–6 metric cards) that change with filters

### Visual language

- Consistent colour semantics:
  - Red / strong warning → Missing, non-compliant, critical anomalies
  - Amber → Under-utilised, refresh due soon, data-quality issues
  - Green / neutral → Healthy, in use, compliant
- Prefer horizontal bar charts for ranked lists (locations, models)
- Prefer line / area for trends over time (purchase cohorts, forecast)
- Tables always include asset_tag + key diagnostic columns and support download

---

## 7. Page Specifications

### 7.1 Executive Overview

**Purpose:** 30-second health check for a Technology / Finance stakeholder or hiring manager.

**KPI cards (examples):**
- Total assets
- Total purchase cost (NZD)
- % Missing or Unassigned
- % Non-compliant
- % Under-utilised (below threshold)
- Assets due for refresh in next 12 months
- Estimated recoverable value from idle / reclaimable assets (simple calculation)

**Visuals:**
- Asset count and cost by `asset_type` (bar or stacked)
- Asset distribution by `lifecycle_stage` (funnel or horizontal bars)
- Top 10 locations by asset count or by problem rate (missing + unassigned + non-compliant)
- Simple trend: assets purchased by year/quarter

**Narrative / insight box:**
- 3–5 bullet auto-generated insights (rule-based is fine for v1), e.g.  
  “12% of laptops are unassigned or missing. Estimated annual idle cost ≈ $X.”  
  “Refresh peak expected in 2027 (Y devices).”

**Interaction:** Global filters apply. Clicking a problem KPI can deep-link or instruct the user to visit the relevant detail page.

---

### 7.2 Asset Inventory

**Purpose:** Searchable, filterable master list — the digital equivalent of “what do we own and where is it?”

**Features:**
- Full filtered dataframe with column selector (show/hide)
- Search box (asset_tag, serial_number, assigned_to, ci_name)
- Summary counts by asset_type, install_status, location
- Ability to download the current view as CSV
- Optional: “Group by location” or “Group by model” summary tables

**Key columns to surface by default:**  
asset_tag, asset_type, model, manufacturer, install_status, lifecycle_stage, assigned_to, location, purchase_date, purchase_cost_nzd, utilisation_score, is_non_compliant

This page supports the “maintaining accurate asset records” and remote-audit preparation aspects of the role.

---

### 7.3 Data Quality & Anomalies

**Purpose:** Explicitly demonstrate data-management and anomaly-detection skills.

**Sections:**
1. **Data quality scorecard**  
   - % complete for critical fields (serial_number, assigned_to, location, purchase_date, etc.)  
   - Count of blank assigned_to, blank location, blank serial  
   - Count of duplicate serial_numbers  
   - Count of date anomalies (future purchase_date, warranty before purchase, etc.)

2. **Anomaly lists** (filterable tables)  
   - Duplicate serials (show both rows)  
   - Missing critical fields  
   - Cost outliers (e.g. > 3× median for that asset_type)  
   - Date inconsistencies  

3. **Simple visual**  
   - Completeness heatmap or bar chart by field  
   - Anomaly volume by location or asset_type

**Insight:**  
“These are the exact data-quality issues an analyst investigates before trusting reports or starting a refresh programme.”

---

### 7.4 Missing / Unassigned / Under-utilised

**Purpose:** Core investigative page that maps directly to the role’s “investigating missing, unassigned, underutilised…” responsibility.

**Three clear tabs or sections:**

**A. Missing assets**  
- Filter: `install_status == "Missing"`  
- Table + count by location / asset_type  
- Days since last seen distribution  
- Total purchase cost at risk  

**B. Unassigned assets**  
- `assigned_to` blank (and usually still “Installed” or in stock)  
- Same breakdowns  
- Highlight devices that are both unassigned and high value  

**C. Under-utilised / stale**  
- Configurable via sidebar thresholds (`utilisation_score`, `days_since_last_seen`)  
- Ranked list of reclaim candidates  
- Estimated opportunity value (sum of residual_value or a simple % of purchase cost)

**Common elements:**  
- “Investigation priority” score or simple ranking (high cost + long time missing/unseen)  
- Export list for follow-up with village managers  
- Short guidance text: “Typical next steps: contact location, raise ServiceNow task, schedule remote or on-site audit.”

---

### 7.5 Lifecycle & Refresh Planning

**Purpose:** Show end-to-end lifecycle visibility and support technology refresh programmes.

**Visuals & content:**
- Lifecycle stage distribution (counts and cost)
- Age pyramid or histogram of `asset_age_years` by asset_type
- Refresh forecast: count and estimated replacement cost by `refresh_year` (next 1–3 years)
- Devices already in “Refresh Due” stage — detailed list
- Warranty status vs age
- Disposal summary (method mix, residual value recovered vs original cost) for retired/disposed assets

**KPI ideas:**  
- Average age by asset_type  
- % of estate past useful life  
- Planned refresh volume next 12 / 24 months  
- Residual value still on books for retired devices

This page supports budgeting conversations and refresh programme planning.

---

### 7.6 Cost Savings & Forecasting

**Purpose:** Turn asset data into financial insight for Finance and Technology leadership.

**Analyses:**
- Total historical spend by year, by asset_type, by location
- Cost of “problem” assets (Missing + Unassigned + low utilisation)
- Simple reclaim / savings scenarios:
  - “If we reclaim 50% of under-utilised devices…”  
  - “If we standardise on top 3 laptop models…” (model proliferation view)
- Refresh cost forecast (using average recent purchase cost × forecast volumes)
- Residual value opportunity on devices approaching or past disposal

**Visuals:**  
- Spend over time  
- Waterfall or bar showing potential savings buckets  
- Model concentration (Pareto) — how many models drive 80% of the estate

**Narrative box:**  
Rule-based or templated recommendations that an analyst might put in a monthly pack.

---

### 7.7 Compliance & Risk

**Purpose:** Surface non-compliant and higher-risk assets.

**Content:**
- Overall compliance rate (`is_non_compliant`)
- Breakdown by reason proxy: encryption Disabled, OS Unsupported, unassigned but in use, past warranty on critical types, etc.
- Non-compliant assets by location and asset_type
- Warranty expired but still “In Use”
- List of devices with notes indicating compliance issues

**KPI cards:**  
- % Non-compliant  
- Count of encryption = Disabled  
- Count of OS = Unsupported  
- High-value non-compliant assets (cost threshold)

Supports governance, audit readiness, and risk conversations.

---

## 8. Key Calculations & Business Rules (v1)

Document these so the implementer does not invent conflicting logic:

| Concept | Rule (v1) |
|---------|-----------|
| Unassigned | `assigned_to` is null, NaN, or empty string |
| Missing | `install_status == "Missing"` |
| Under-utilised | `utilisation_score < utilisation_threshold` (default 30, sidebar controlled) |
| Stale | `days_since_last_seen > stale_threshold` (default 90) |
| Non-compliant | Use source `is_non_compliant` flag; optionally also surface encryption/OS fields |
| Asset age | `(today - purchase_date).days / 365.25` |
| Reclaim candidate | Unassigned OR Missing OR (Under-utilised AND still In Use / Installed) |
| Estimated idle / opportunity value | For v1 use `residual_value_nzd` where available, otherwise a conservative % of `purchase_cost_nzd` (e.g. 15–25% for under-utilised, higher for missing). Document the chosen heuristic in the UI. |
| Refresh due soon | `lifecycle_stage == "Refresh Due"` OR `remaining_life_years <= 0.5` OR `refresh_year == current_year` |

All thresholds that users can change must be visible and labelled.

---

## 9. Non-Functional Requirements

- **Performance:** 15k–25k rows must feel responsive with caching. Avoid full re-computation on every widget change where possible.
- **Responsiveness:** Usable on a laptop screen; wide layout preferred.
- **Accessibility / clarity:** High-contrast KPI cards, clear labels, no unexplained abbreviations.
- **Reproducibility:** With a fixed CSV (or fixed Supabase snapshot) the numbers must be stable.
- **Documentation inside the app:** Every page has a short “What this page is for” expander linking back to the role activity it supports.
- **No real PII:** Data is synthetic; still treat `assigned_to` as if it were sensitive in any future extension.

---

## 10. Implementation Guidance for the Future Developer

1. Start with a solid `data_loader.py` that returns a clean pandas DataFrame and a source label.
2. Centralise derived columns and business rules in `metrics.py` so every page uses the same definitions.
3. Build Executive Overview and Missing/Unassigned pages first — they deliver the most role-relevant impact quickly.
4. Keep charts simple and labelled. Prefer clarity over novelty.
5. Use Streamlit session state for filter persistence across pages if needed.
6. Provide a `requirements.txt` and a short `DASHBOARD_README.md` for running the app.
7. Do not hard-code Ryman-specific branding beyond what already exists in the synthetic data; keep the app presentable as a generic ITAM demo that happens to use this dataset.

---

## 11. Success Criteria (Definition of Done for v1)

The project can be considered complete when:

- [ ] All seven pages listed above exist and load without error from both CSV and Supabase (when configured)
- [ ] Global filters work and update KPIs/charts consistently
- [ ] Data-quality issues, missing, unassigned, under-utilised, and non-compliant assets are clearly visible and exportable
- [ ] Lifecycle stage and refresh forecast are visible and numerically consistent with the source fields
- [ ] A non-technical stakeholder can understand the main message of the Executive Overview in under two minutes
- [ ] The app contains in-page text that explicitly links each major view back to the Asset Management Analyst responsibilities
- [ ] Code is organised, commented, and runnable with the documented environment variables / CSV

---

## 12. Out of Scope (explicitly)

- Writing back to ServiceNow or updating Supabase rows from the UI
- User login / role-based access
- Predictive ML models beyond simple rule-based flags (can be a v2 experiment)
- Pixel-perfect recreation of ServiceNow UI
- Real Ryman data or any non-synthetic data
- Mobile-first redesign

---

## 13. Future Enhancement Ideas (v2+)

- Site Audit Simulator: select a village → generate a checklist of assets that should be verified
- Natural-language question box (“Which locations have the most missing laptops?”) powered by a lightweight LLM or even rule-based parsing
- Scenario modelling (“What if useful life of laptops is extended to 5 years?”)
- Scheduled email-style summary export
- Comparison of two time snapshots (requires historical data generation)
